description: Common-mode bias return, one per in-amp input
notes: REPLACES R-PD-BREATH. Without these the in-amp floats when unplugged and saturates to a rail. ~60nA against a 350mA power return = 0.2ppm, so AGND's no-current rule survives

description: Pitch gain trimmer, in series with R2 of the LT5400 pair
notes: 200R, not 1k. In series with R2, against R-GAIN-CTR's 100R in series with R1: the ratio is 1 at mid-travel and the trim is +/-1% - BIPOLAR, because the DAC's gain error is (+/-0.15% of FSR max, SBAS430E p.3) and the LT5400's absolute value cannot be leaned on. At mid-travel its ~100ppm/degC acts on 100R of 10k, ~1ppm/degC of ratio, comparable to the LT5400. CW END STRAPPED TO THE WIPER on the sheet, so a dirty track fails to a known resistance rather than open. Bourns 3296W-1-201LF

description: Pitch offset trimmer, AHEAD of the VREFOUT follower
notes: ACROSS VREFOUT AND AGND_MOD, ITS WIPER INJECTING INTO THE REFERENCE FOLLOWER through R-VREF-INJ against R-VREF-SER, with the follower at gain 1.02 (R-VREF-FB/R-VREF-GND): 2.500V at mid-travel, about -60/+50mV of span - 72 cents of intercept one way and 60 the other. It touches the gain (1 + k) NOT AT ALL. Its 10k to ground is also what holds VREFOUT at 0V while the DAC's reference is disabled and the pin is 3-state. The network and its drift are on pitch-stage.md. Bourns 3296W-1-103LF

description: Compensation cap, op-amp OUTPUT to the inverting input
notes: FROM THE OP-AMP OUTPUT TO THE (-) INPUT. NOT 'across the feedback resistor' - with the tap at the jack, R2 spans jack-to-(-), so a cap across R2 connects the same two nodes and leaves R-OUT-PROT inside the loop at every frequency: 18 degrees of phase margin with 2m of cable, under 10 with four destinations. Three documents said 'across R2' and were wrong. 2.2nF with C-FILT-PITCH restored is maximally flat, -3dB at 12.2kHz. IT IS NOT A FILTER: a cap in the feedback of a NON-INVERTING stage gives (2+sRC)/(1+sRC), a pole and a zero an octave up, flattening at unity - 6.02dB maximum for any value. Two independent reviews found this separately

description: Anti-alias/glitch filter on the pitch DAC input, ahead of the op-amp
notes: THE ACTUAL PITCH FILTER. 15.9kHz against R-OPAMP-IN's 1k, on a node with NO LOOP AROUND IT. C-FB-PITCH cannot do this job: a cap across the feedback resistor of a NON-INVERTING stage gives (2+sRC)/(1+sRC) - a pole at 7.2kHz (R2 + TRIM-GAIN against 2.2nF) and a zero an octave above, flattening at unity, so 6.02dB of attenuation maximum for any value. It is a shelf, not a pole. Filtering the DAC before the stage is also what the surveyed designs do

description: Reconstruction and RF shunt at the pitch jack
notes: RESTORED. It was deleted on the reasoning that a cap on the feedback node sits inside the DC loop at the handover; two independent loop analyses then put 10nF there and found phase margin UNCHANGED, because C-FB-PITCH ties the (-) input to the op-amp OUTPUT so beta(inf)=1 and R-OUT-PROT isolates the jack above the handover. The feedback network is a LEAD at every load tried - open, 200pF, 800pF, 10nF, dead short. Deleting it cost 30dB at 1MHz and left the connector with no low-impedance shunt at all

description: DC bias path to ground at every DAC output pin
notes: AT THE DAC PIN, not after R-OPAMP-IN - 100k after the 1k would form a divider and cost 1% of gain. Without it the op-amp (+) inputs have no DC path to ground: their only connection is a DAC pin that may be high-Z before power-on reset, so outputs can sit at either rail during that window. The identical problem was already found and fixed on the breath in-amp (R-BIAS-INAMP); this is the same fix on the six DAC-driven nodes

description: Matched resistor network for pitch scaling
package: MSOP-8 MS8E (0.65mm pitch) WITH 1.88 x 1.68mm EXPOSED PAD
notes: RATIO IS 1:1 - the pitch stage is a non-inverting amp with the reference at the bottom of the feedback divider (see pitch-stage.md). Two of four sections used. ORDER CODE IS TWO LETTER FIELDS: LT5400 + <A|B matching> + <C|I|H|MP temp> + MS8E-1#PBF. The -1 option is the four-equal-10k 1:1 quad and THERE IS NO 1:3 OPTION [p.2 table: -1 10k 1:1, -2 100k 1:1, -3 1:10, -4 1k 1:1, -5 1M 1:1, -6 1:5]. Grade A is 0.01% matching, B 0.025%; A degrades to +/-0.0125% over -40/+85degC while B is flat. MUST BE THE MS8 (MSOP) OPTION, NOT THE LEADLESS DFN. *** MS8E HAS AN EXPOSED PAD *** [p.2, p.8] - the footprint is MSOP-8-1EP_3x3mm_P0.65mm_EP1.68x1.88mm, NOT a plain MSOP-8. WHERE THE PAD GOES [p.6]: not DC-connected to any resistor, 'do not tie the exposed pad to noisy signals or noisy grounds', 'connecting the exposed pad to a quiet AC ground is recommended'. THE PAD GOES TO AGND_MOD (pitch-stage.md, 'The LT5400's exposed pad'): pad-to-resistor coupling is 5.5 pF against 1.4 pF resistor-to-resistor, so the pad is the dominant stray on the 1V/oct node. The sheet's symbol carries it as pin 9, EP. The two spare sections are tied to AGND_MOD at both ends. Ratio tracking 1 ppm/degC MAX (0.2 typ). ABSOLUTE tolerance is +/-7.5% (A) / +/-15% (B), which sets TRIM-GAIN's real authority, +/-100/(R + 100) about R-GAIN-CTR, at +/-0.86% to +/-1.16% on the B part rather than a nominal +/-1% - still several times the DAC's +/-0.15% FSR gain error (SBAS430E p.3). WHY THE PART IS KEPT, since its own tempco is currently masked: the DAC's internal reference drifts 0.42 cents over 10degC and cannot be trimmed, against 0.027 for the LT5400 and 0.38 for two 0.1%/10ppm discretes - $8 permanently solves the one term that can be, on a board built once, and attacking the reference later is only worth doing if the network is already there. CAVEAT FOR ANYONE EDITING ADR 0006: the banked rev fa's option table ends at -6, so LT5400-7 and 'a 1:4 offered directly' are NOT-IN-DOCUMENT rather than refuted - do not 'correct' ADR 0006 by citing rev fa's silence. 5400fc.pdf is still wanted. ORDERED AS LT5400BIMS8E-1#PBF [p.3 order table]: B GRADE because the static ratio error is trimmed out by TRIM-GAIN and B's 0.025% is flat over temperature where A's 0.01% degrades to 0.0125% - the drift, not the initial match, is what is left after trim, and it is the same 0.2 ppm/C for both; I GRADE (-40 to +85 C) for the rack in a van, as U-LOADSW. LCSC C42416907, 16 in stock at $11.61 [web LCSC 2026-09-30]

description: Centres TRIM-GAIN: 100R in series with the LT5400's R1
notes: Half of TRIM-GAIN's 200R, in the other leg, so the ratio is exactly 1 at the trimmer's mid-travel and the trim is bipolar. Thin film, 25 ppm/C. RT0805BRD07100RL, LCSC C110773

description: VREFOUT into the pitch reference follower's (+) input
notes: Two jobs: with R-VREF-INJ it sets the fraction of V_ref the offset trim can move, and it is the follower's clamp-current protection, as R-OPAMP-IN is for the channels. THIN FILM, 25 ppm/C, NOT R-OPAMP-IN's part: it is half of a ratio that sets V_ref, and V_ref is the intercept. RT0805BRD071KL, LCSC C110774

description: TRIM-OFFSET's wiper into the pitch reference follower
notes: About 4% of V_ref is all the trimmer can reach, so its tempco and its wiper act on 4%. Thin film, 25 ppm/C. RT0805BRD0722K1L, LCSC C865310

description: Pitch reference follower, output to (-) input
notes: With R-VREF-GND, gain 1.02: puts 2.500V back at TRIM-OFFSET's mid-travel. The ratio's drift reaches V_ref scaled by 0.02/1.02. Thin film, 25 ppm/C. RT0805BRD07200RL, LCSC C865287

description: Pitch reference follower, (-) input to AGND_MOD
notes: Partner of R-VREF-FB. Thin film, 25 ppm/C. RT0805BRD0710KL, LCSC C110775

description: Jack-side ESD clamp on the pitch jack tip, ahead of the LT5400
notes: BIDIRECTIONAL, TIP TO SLEEVE, AT THE PITCH JACK ON THE MODULE JACK BOARD - not on module-main, so a strike is clamped before it crosses J-B2B-MOD. WHY: the jack tip reaches RN-PITCH's R2 through TRIM-GAIN's 0-200R and nothing else, and the LT5400 has no internal ESD diodes: +/-1kV HBM, 'ESD beyond this voltage can damage or degrade the device including causing pin-to-pin shorts' [LT5400.pdf p.6]; its Figure 1 offers diodes to the rails or 'bidirectional Zeners to ground' at the connector, and the jack board has no rails. MUST BE BIDIRECTIONAL with standoff above 12V: the jack swings -2.5 to +7.5V and a patch can put another module's +/-12V on it; a unidirectional part would conduct at -0.7V. PESD15VL1BA [NEXPERIA-PESD15VL1BA.pdf p.4]: VRWM 15V; VBR 17.1V min at 5mA; IRM 50nA max at 15V; Cd 16pF typ at 0V; VCL 25V at 1A, 44V at IPPM 5A (8/20us); IEC 61000-4-2 30kV contact [p.3]. 44V is inside the LT5400's 80V across any two pins [LT5400.pdf p.2]. NO ACCURACY COST: it sits on JACK_TIP, which is the DC feedback node, so its leakage is a load inside the loop like any VCO (zero error), and 16pF beside C-FILT-PITCH's 10nF is 0.16 percent of it, inside that part's own tolerance; pitch-stage/sim runs the stage with it fitted. Returns to AGND_MOD at the jack sleeve, not to a rail, so it cannot back-power the module the way a rail clamp at the jack did (D-JACK-CLAMP). Nexperia PESD15VL1BA,115, LCSC C85378, JLC extended part
